corrected_value.authors: Wang YM, Ma L, Lu SY, Chan TCY, Yam JCS, Tang SM, et al.
corrected_value.title: Analysis of multiple genetic loci reveals MPDZ-NF1B rs1324183 as a putative genetic marker for keratoconus.

decisions.quote:
In recently years, Wang YM and Hao XD et al. both analyzed the association of SNP locus with keratoconus in Chinese population, and revealed that the rs1324183 (
MPDZ-NF1B
), which located between the
MPDZ
and
NF1B
genes, is a putative genetic marker for monitoring the progression of keratoconus and should be further investigated in other different Chinese populations [
23
,
24
]. Thence, in this study, we collected a total of 114 KC patients who live in northwestern of China for the first time and further confirmed the association between the rs1324183 (
MPDZ-NF1B
) and KC, providing a clear basis for early clinical diagnosis in Chinese population.
decisions.reason: Yuan et al. (2022) collect new genotype data from 114 keratoconus patients and 88 controls in Ningxia (northwestern China) to replicate the Chinese-population genetic association between MPDZ-NF1B SNP rs1324183 and keratoconus reported by both Hao XD et al. (2015) [23] and Wang YM et al. (2018) [24], and directly compare their replicated risk-allele and risk-genotype findings against both studies in the Discussion. Shipped row 790 covers only Hao et al. (2015) (Ophthalmic Genetics 36(2): 132-136, doi: 10.3109/13816810.2015.1005317, blind target 0). Reference [24] (Wang YM et al., 2018, Br J Ophthalmol 102(12): 1736-1741, doi: 10.1136/bjophthalmol-2018-312218) is an independent empirical study by a different research group in a separate cohort, not an alternate report of Hao et al. (2015), and is missing from the shipped rows.
